themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints surged to 20 this week versus a baseline of 3.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 515% spike (z-score: 10.22)—signaling a sudden deterioration in public safety perception or incident reporting in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 20 non-emergency police complaints filed this week vs. 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (515% increase)
Z-score of 10.22 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
This is the most recent and most severe spike in the dataset
reporting_angles: Report on what specific incidents drove the 20-complaint surge—interview NYPD and residents on the ground
Investigate whether residents are newly reporting crimes or if actual incidents have increased; compare to crime data from NYC Police Department
Examine whether the spike correlates with school holidays, weather events, or other external factors this week

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints surged in the past 2 weeks—missing signs up 1100% (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average) and damaged signs up 380% (3 complaints last week vs. 0.6 average)—alongside a 300% spike in obstruction complaints (14 last week vs. 3.5 average), suggesting rapid deterioration of public street infrastructure.
evidence: Street sign missing complaints: 3 this period vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
Street sign damaged complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% increase, z-score: 4.91)
Obstruction complaints: 14 last week vs. 3.5 weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 6.33)
Three distinct infrastructure categories spiking simultaneously suggests systemic maintenance issue
reporting_angles: Map the locations of missing and damaged signs—are they concentrated in specific neighborhoods or corridors?
Interview NYC Department of Transportation about maintenance schedules and whether they've deprioritized Bed-Stuy
Report on how obstruction complaints connect to sidewalk safety and accessibility issues, particularly for elderly residents

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes & Street Clutter
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 4 two weeks ago versus 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 6.97), and tree requests jumped to 3 last week from 0.1 baseline (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69), both suggesting rapid degradation of public space aesthetics or micromobility infrastructure mismanagement.
evidence: Abandoned bike complaints: 4 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 6.97)
New tree requests: 3 (last week) vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Both spikes are recent (within 2 weeks) and statistically extreme
reporting_angles: Investigate whether bikeshare bikes (Citi Bike) are being abandoned at higher rates; interview company on enforcement
Report on the tree request spike—is this new demand for greening, or a sign that existing trees are dying/missing?
Connect to long-standing community board request for parks and amenities—do residents feel public space is being neglected?

themes_detail.label: Litter & Dirty Conditions Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints jumped to 102 three weeks ago versus 38.2 weekly average (167% increase, z-score: 4.44), and litter basket requests spiked to 6 three weeks ago from 1.4 average (336% increase), suggesting acute sanitation challenges concentrated in a narrow timeframe.
evidence: Dirty condition complaints: 102 (3 weeks ago) vs. 38.2 weekly average (167% increase, z-score: 4.44)
Litter basket request complaints: 6 (3 weeks ago) vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% increase, z-score: 4.66)
Both spikes occurred simultaneously 3 weeks ago, suggesting a common trigger (event, policy change, or service interruption)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYC Sanitation reduced service levels or collection frequency in Bed-Stuy around that date
Interview residents about whether the dirty conditions spike corresponded to holiday disruptions or weather events
Report on whether the community board's recurring request for enhanced sanitation remains unfunded or deprioritized

themes_detail.label: Ongoing Heat/Hot Water Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dominate the 90-day complaint volume (3,696 total), representing the single largest maintenance-related burden for Bed-Stuy residents, though this appears to be a chronic issue rather than a new spike—indicating a long-running systemic problem in building infrastructure.
evidence: 3,696 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (highest category by far, 1.5x the next highest complaint type)
No statistical spike detected (suggesting chronic baseline rather than new crisis), but volume indicates endemic problem
Heat/hot water is the #1 concern by complaint volume across the entire district
reporting_angles: Conduct investigative series on Bed-Stuy's aging rental stock—are specific buildings or blocks repeat offenders?
Interview tenants about enforcement gaps: why do complaints persist without penalty for landlords?
Report on whether city housing inspection capacity is adequate to enforce building code violations in this high-complaint district
